questions.q: What are the three tiers of the Panchayati Raj system in India?
questions.a: The three tiers are the Gram Panchayat (village level), the Panchayat Samiti (block level), and the Zila Parishad (district level). A wrong answer here suggests the student is confusing local government with national or state government structures.

questions.q: Who is the head of the Gram Panchayat, and how is this person chosen?
questions.a: The head is called the Sarpanch or Pradhan, and they are elected by the members of the Gram Sabha. If a student says the government appoints them, they misunderstand the core democratic nature of the institution.

questions.q: If a village needs a new handpump for water, which level of the Panchayati Raj system would likely handle the initial request?
questions.a: The Gram Panchayat handles this. The steps include: 1) Identifying the need, 2) Raising it in a Gram Sabha meeting, 3) The Gram Panchayat deciding on the project. An incorrect answer suggests the student thinks all decisions are made by distant authorities.

questions.q: How does the "bottom-up" structure of the Panchayati Raj help in governing a large country like India?
questions.a: It allows local problems to be solved by people who actually live there and understand the context. A wrong answer shows the student does not grasp why local participation is more efficient than centralized control.

questions.q: Is it better to have a single leader decide everything in a village, or to have a Gram Sabha discuss and decide?
questions.a: A Gram Sabha is better because it represents the voice of the community, ensuring fairness and collective agreement. A preference for a single leader indicates a misunderstanding of the democratic process of inclusion.

questions.q: Design a simple campaign poster for a candidate running for Sarpanch. What are the two most important issues you would include?
questions.a: The poster should focus on local needs like sanitation, water, or education. A poor answer focuses on national issues (like defense or foreign policy) that fall outside the scope of a Gram Panchayat.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The ______ Raj is a three-tier system of local self-government in rural India designed to allow villagers to manage their own affairs.

Fill in the blank: Imagine your village street light is broken, or a ______ school wall needs urgent repairs; would you write a letter to the Prime Minister in New Delhi, or talk to someone in your own village?
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to identify the three tiers of the system, name the elected head of the Gram Panchayat, and list at least three primary responsibilities of local village government.
